name: Renode script
comment: Grammar for Renode Monitor scripts, following https://renode.readthedocs.io/en/latest/basic/monitor-syntax.html . Note that `emulation`, `machine`, `sysbus` and `connector` are objects in the Monitor's object tree rather than commands, so they are scoped as classes and the CamelCase token after one of them as a method. `:` is a comment prefix, which is what makes the `:name:` / `:description:` metadata and its continuation lines comments.

metadata.comment: Script metadata. These are ordinary `:` comments with a convention, and Renode reads them to describe the script.

patterns.comment: A bare `:` also starts a comment — used to continue a :description: across lines.
patterns.name: comment.line.documentation.renode-resc

macroContinuation.comment: Lines of a multi-line `macro` body are introduced with `>`.

multilineString.comment: Triple-quoted string, most often a `macro` body. Embedded `python "..."` inside still highlights.
multilineString.name: string.quoted.triple.renode-resc

pythonInline.comment: `python "..."` runs a Python statement in the Monitor's interpreter — highlight the argument as Python.

backtick.comment: Command substitution: the inner command runs first and its result is spliced in.

pathLiteral.comment: `@path` is Renode's path literal (it enables completion). $ORIGIN/$CWD-relative paths deliberately take no `@`.

patterns.comment: $ORIGIN = the including script's directory (scripts only); $CWD = the working directory (Monitor only).
patterns.name: variable.language.renode-resc

patterns.comment: An explicitly scoped variable. Unqualified names bind to the SELECTED MACHINE's scope, which is why cross-machine scripts use $global.

assignment.comment: `?=` assigns only if unset (how a script declares an overridable default); `=` always assigns.
assignment.name: keyword.operator.assignment.renode-resc

commandAliases.comment: Single-letter aliases (i=include, s=start, p=pause, q=quit) — only at the start of a line, so they cannot swallow a stray letter elsewhere.

commands.comment: Built-in Monitor commands (class list from renode-infrastructure src/UserInterface/Commands).
commands.name: keyword.other.command.renode-resc

builtinObjects.comment: Roots of the Monitor's object tree, not commands — `emulation CreateX`, `sysbus LoadBinary` are method calls on these.
builtinObjects.name: support.class.renode-resc

objectTarget.comment: A user-named object being addressed, i.e. a lowercase first token followed by a CamelCase method: `medium SetPosition ...`, `term WriteChar ...`.

methodCall.comment: A CamelCase token is a method or property on the object to its left.
methodCall.name: entity.name.function.renode-resc
